arxiv-2012-14027.title: Data-Driven Fractional Subgrid-scale Modeling for Scalar Turbulence: A Nonlocal LES Approach Journal: Journal of Computational Physics
arxiv-2012-14027.creator: Ali Akhavan-Safaei, Mehdi Samiee, Mohsen Zayernouri
arxiv-2012-14027.description: Abstract Filtering the passive scalar transport equation in the large-eddy simulation (LES) of turbulent transport gives rise to the closure term corresponding to the unresolved scalar flux. Understanding and respecting the statistical features of subgrid-scale (SGS) flux is a crucial point in robustness and predictability of the LES.

arxiv-2102-03043.title: The Refined Assortment Optimization Problem
arxiv-2102-03043.creator: Gerardo Berbeglia, Alvaro Flores, Guillermo Gallego
arxiv-2102-03043.description: Abstract We introduce the refined assortment optimization problem where a firm may decide to make some of its products harder to get instead of making them unavailable as in the traditional assortment optimization problem. Airlines, for example, offer fares with severe restrictions rather than making them unavailable.

arxiv-2401-14430.title: A Westervelt equation for acoustic wave propagation through weakly stratified, arbitrary Mach number atmospheres
arxiv-2401-14430.creator: Liam J. Tope, Jae Wook Kim, Peter Spence
arxiv-2401-14430.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Liam J. Tope, Jae Wook Kim, Peter Spence. Nonlinear distortion of infrasonic waves through atmospheres up to thermospheric altitudes govern large-range ground-level observations of explosive noise sources, causing large differences between the near and far field. Propagation modelling in this scenario to include realistic nonlinear effects has thus far been limited to high-fidelity, numerically intensive Direct Numerical Simulations of the Navier-Stokes equations, or nonlinear parabolic equations with restrictions on the mean flow Mach number.

arxiv-2402-13043.title: Effective and Efficient Conversation Retrieval for Dialogue State Tracking with Implicit Text Summaries
arxiv-2402-13043.creator: Seanie Lee Jianpeng Cheng Joris Driesen Alexandru Coca Anders Johannsen
arxiv-2402-13043.description: Abstract Few-shot dialogue state tracking (DST) with Large Language Models (LLM) relies on an effective and efficient conversation retriever to find similar in-context examples for prompt learning. Previous works use raw dialogue context as search keys and queries, and a retriever is fine-tuned with annotated dialogues to achieve superior performance.

arxiv-2404-04737.title: A free boundary problem for an immersed filament in 3D Stokes flow
arxiv-2404-04737.creator: Laurel Ohm
arxiv-2404-04737.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Laurel Ohm. We consider a simplified extensible version of a dynamic free boundary problem for a thin filament with radius ϵ > 0 \epsilon>0 immersed in 3D Stokes flow. The 3D fluid is coupled to the quasi-1D filament dynamics via a novel type of angle-averaged Neumann-to-Dirichlet operator for the Stokes equations, and much of the difficulty in the analysis lies in understanding this operator.

arxiv-2409-19415.title: Bridging the Gap in Hybrid Decision-Making Systems
arxiv-2409-19415.creator: Federico Mazzoni, Roberto Pellungrini, Riccardo Guidotti ✉
arxiv-2409-19415.description: Abstract We introduce Bridget , a novel human-in-the-loop system for hybrid decision-making, aiding the user to label records from an un-labeled dataset, attempting to “bridge the gap” between the two most popular Hybrid Decision-Making paradigms: those featuring the human in a leading position, and the other with a machine making most of the decisions.

arxiv-2504-05326.title: Totally Disjoint 3-Digit Decimal Check Digit Codes Thanks: ©The author, dunning@bgsu.edu, grants copyright permissionsas specified in Creative Commons License CC BY-SA 4.0. (See Endnote 2)
arxiv-2504-05326.creator: Larry A. Dunning
arxiv-2504-05326.description: Abstract Abstract: In 1969 J. Verhoeff provided the first examples of a decimal error detecting code using a single check digit to provide protection against all single, transposition and adjacent twin errors. The three versions of such a code that he presented are length 3-digit codes with 2 information digits.

arxiv-2505-02083.title: On the dimension of orbits of matrix pencils under strict equivalence
arxiv-2505-02083.creator: Fernando De Terán, Froilán M. Dopico, Patryk Pagacz
arxiv-2505-02083.description: Abstract We prove that, given two matrix pencils L L and M M , if M M belongs to the closure of the orbit of L L under strict equivalence, then the dimension of the orbit of M M is smaller than or equal to the dimension of the orbit of L L , and the equality is only attained

arxiv-2505-03215.title: High-Harmonic Generation and Optical Torque Interaction via Relativistic Diffraction of a Spatiotemporal Vortex Light
arxiv-2505-03215.creator: Ke Hu, Xinju Guo, Longqing Yi
arxiv-2505-03215.description: Abstract Diffraction of a relativistically-strong light can produce high-order harmonics via the “relativistic oscillating window” mechanism. In this process, the characteristics of the 2D electron dynamics at the diffraction screen can be imprinted to the generated harmonics, which provides abundant opportunities for manipulating light-matter interaction.

arxiv-2506-21735.title: Equitable Federated Learning with NCA
arxiv-2506-21735.creator: Nick Lemke 1,, Mirko Konstantin 0, Henry John Krumb, John Kalkhof, Jonathan Stieber, Anirban Mukhopadhyay
arxiv-2506-21735.description: Abstract Federated Learning (FL) is enabling collaborative model training across institutions without sharing sensitive patient data. This approach is particularly valuable in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where access to trained medical professionals is limited. However, FL adoption in LMICs faces significant barriers, including limited high-performance computing resources and unreliable internet connectivity.

arxiv-2508-17589.title: Polarization Observables T T and F F in the γ ​ p → π 0 ​ p \gamma p\to\pi^{0}p Reaction at CLAS
arxiv-2508-17589.creator: H. Jiang, S. Strauch, I.I. Strakovsky, D. Rönchen, R. Workman, P. Achenbach, J. S. Alvarado, H. Atac, L. Baashen, N.A. Baltzell, L. Barion, M. Bashkanov, M. Battaglieri, F. Benmokhtar, A. Bianconi, A.S. Biselli, M. Bondi, F. Bossù, S. Boiarinov, K.-T. Brinkmann, W.J. Briscoe, W.K. Brooks, V.D. Burke
arxiv-2508-17589.description: Abstract Pion photoproduction in the γ → ​ p → → π 0 ​ p \overrightarrow{\gamma}\overrightarrow{p}\to\pi^{0}p reaction has been measured in the FROST experiment at the Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility. In this experiment, circularly polarized photons with energies up to 3.082 GeV impinged on a transversely polarized frozen-spin target. Final-state protons were detected in the CEBAF Large Acceptance Spectrometer.

In the interview, Grossi expressed both optimism and pessimism about the nuclear landscape: he was hopefu

pmc-10511798.title: A method for in vivo evaluation of α-glucosidase inhibition using Drosophila
pmc-10511798.creator: Nattapong Wongchum, Alongklod Tanomtong, Somchai Pinlaor, Chatmongkon Suwannapoom, Ananya Dechakhamphu
pmc-10511798.description: The development of α-glucosidase inhibitors is essential for the prevention of type II diabetes. Previous research has investigated in vitro inhibition using isolated α-glucosidase, which may not accurately reflect physical processes. The method presented in this study aims to establish a rapid and inexpensive in vivo method to study the inhibition of α-glucosidase activity using Drosophila as a model organism.

pmc-10625671.title: Allogenic Umbilical Cord Tissue as a Scaffold for Ankle Osteoarthritis
pmc-10625671.creator: Ashim Gupta, Adarsh Aratikatla
pmc-10625671.description: Osteoarthritis (OA) of ankle followed by injury to the talus is one of the most common disorders of ankle. Traditional treatment modalities have limitations and do not address the etiopathogenetic cause of OA. Perinatal tissue-derived biologics such as umbilical cords have shown potential for musculoskeletal regenerative medicine applications.

pmc-11678346.title: The Beneficial Roles of Seaweed in Atopic Dermatitis
pmc-11678346.creator: Ah-Reum Kim, Myeong-Jin Kim, Jaeseong Seo, Kyoung Mi Moon, Bonggi Lee, Javier Ávila-Román
pmc-11678346.description: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic, inflammatory skin condition characterized by severe pruritus and recurrent flare-ups, significantly impacting patients’ quality of life. Current treatments, such as corticosteroids and immunomodulators, often provide symptomatic relief but can lead to adverse effects with prolonged use.

pmc-11960324.title: Smith-Kingsmore syndrome with nystagmus as the initial symptom
pmc-11960324.creator: Meiling Cai, Yanfei Zhao, He Wang, Shicheng Liu, Huiyi Jiang
pmc-11960324.description: BackgroundSmith-Kingsmore syndrome (SKS) is a rare autosomal dominant disorder caused by de novo mutations of gene MTOR in most cases and germline mosaicism in a few cases. The first case of SKS was reported in 2013. The incidence of SKS remains unknown. The clinical manifestations of SKS are diverse, and common features are macrocephaly, intellectual disability, and seizures.

pmc-12399655.title: Spatial heterogeneity reveals an evolutionary signature predicting therapeutic response and clinical outcomes in hepatocellular carcinoma
pmc-12399655.creator: Shangyi Luo, Li Liu, Yang Sun, Jian Shi, Yajing Zhang
pmc-12399655.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionIntra-tumoral heterogeneity is a prominent characteristic of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, it remains unexplored whether intra-tumoral transcriptomic differences can capture crucial information regarding HCC evolution and be utilized to derive a predictive signature for patient’s clinical trajectories.MethodsWe quantified transcriptomic heterogeneity using four multiregional HCC cohorts comprising 172 samples from 37 patients, and validated transcriptomic heterogeneity and spatial dynamics using multiregional single-cell transcriptomic profiling of 110,817 cells from 34 liver specimens.

pmc-12475692.title: Poster 170: Minimally-Invasive Mid-Substance Posterior Cruciate Ligament Repair Restores Intact-Level Stability: A Biomechanical Study
pmc-12475692.creator: Soheil Sabzevari, Jim Hsu, Isabelle Shen, Steven Tommasini
pmc-12475692.description: Objectives:High-grade, symptomatic posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) tears present a treatment challenge: the PCL’s spontaneous healing potential supports conservative treatment, but excessive laxity is often encountered; PCL reconstruction, however, entails lengthy recovery, increased invasiveness, and variable long-term outcomes, with residual laxity still a liability.

pmc-12698390.title: Editorial: Finding new hope in old treatments: repurposing immunotherapy in transplantation
pmc-12698390.creator: Yeqi Nian, Jasper Iske, Xiaodong Yuan
pmc-12698390.description: imus and cyclosporine in the 1970s represented a major advance, current therapeutic regimens remain insufficient to fully resolve these complex issues, highlighting the ongoing need for innovative approaches (1). Drug repurposing—the application of existing drugs to new clinical indications—has emerged as a promising strategy to accelerate therapeutic discovery in transplantation.

pmc-13093323.title: Safety evaluation of the food enzyme endo‐1,4‐β‐xylanase from the genetically modified Trichoderma reesei strain Dp‐Nzd66
pmc-13093323.creator: EFSA Panel on Food Enzymes (FEZ), Holger Zorn, José Manuel Barat Baviera, Claudia Bolognesi, Francesco Catania, Gabriele Gadermaier, Ralf Greiner, Baltasar Mayo, Alicja Mortensen, Yrjö Henrik Roos, Marize L M Solano, Monika Sramkova, Henk Van Loveren, Laurence Vernis, Jaime Aguiera, Magdalena Andrys
pmc-13093323.description: The food enzyme endo‐1,4‐β‐xylanase (4‐β‐d‐xylan xylanohydrolase; EC 3.2.1.8) is produced with the genetically modified Trichoderma reesei strain DP‐Nzd66 by Genencor International B.V. The genetic modifications do not give rise to safety concerns. The food enzyme was considered free from viable cells of the production organism and its DNA.

pmc-13273859.title: Large language models for generating longitudinal synthetic data in low-risk pregnancy care
pmc-13273859.creator: Gonçalo Pinto, Vítor Crista, Regina Silva, Bruno Costa, Filipe Andrade Bernardi, Rute Almeida, Julio Souza, Alberto Freitas, Goreti Marreiros, Luís Conceição
pmc-13273859.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This article describes an obstetric dataset covering the full continuum of care of 5000 synthetic low-risk pregnant women, from preconception to post-birth follow-up, generated using a large language model with zero-shot prompting. It includes trimester-specific clinical measurements, such as gestational weight, hemoglobin levels, glucose testing, anemia markers, and body mass index, as well as variables intrinsic to perinatal care, including preconception characteristics, antenatal consultations, and delivery outcomes.The dataset was generated through iterative prompt engineering.

pmc-13407797.title: Metabolomics assisted by transcriptomics analysis to reveal metabolic characteristics and potential biomarkers of early-onset colorectal cancer
pmc-13407797.creator: Hui Zhang, Jiangping Yu, Rongwei Ruan, Zhao Cui, Yali Tao, Shuwen Zhu, Shi Wang
pmc-13407797.description: BackgroundMetabolic reprogramming plays a crucial role in the occurrence and progression of colorectal cancer (CRC). However, the relationship between metabolism and CRC development remains to be fully elucidated.MethodsWe collected 45 colorectal tissue samples, including 15 cases of early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC), 15 cases of later-onset colorectal cancer (LOCRC), and 15 adjacent normal tissues for metabolomic analysis.

pmc-13564212.title: History of drug pricing reform in the United States: from policy foundations to latest reforms
pmc-13564212.creator: Sujith Ramachandran, Arman Arabshomali, John Coster
pmc-13564212.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This article examines the historical evolution of prescription drug pricing policy in the United States from the 1960s through 2025, highlighting how incremental reforms have produced a complex and fragmented system. It traces the foundations of drug pricing across Medicaid, Medicare, the Veterans Affairs (VA) system, and the 340B Drug Discount program, emphasizing the development of key pricing benchmarks such as Average Wholesale Price (AWP), Average Manufacturer Price (AMP), and Average Sales Price (ASP).

Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel.
